subject: Lodestar-4b: 503 spike — customer notification, interim mitigations, and post-incident follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightbox.ai>, ops@brightbox.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lodestar-4b: 503 spike — notice + immediate mitigations

Hi Sarah / BrightBox team,

We wanted to notify you that starting ~07:45 PDT this morning we observed an elevated rate of 503/timeout responses for the Lodestar-4b model when handling large batched requests from BrightBox (your account). The spike lasted for roughly 35 minutes and impacted ~9% of generation requests (predominantly multi-turn chat sessions with long context).

What we did immediately:
- Diverted traffic away from the affected Lodestar-4b pool to a warmed fallback variant (Lodestar-4b-compat) to reduce customer-visible failures.
- Temporarily reduced the maximum batch size for your route to keep p95 latency below your SLA target.
- Kicked off collection of request/response samples and runtime telemetry (attached: lodestar-4b-request-samples.txt, cpu metrics).

Current status: service is back to expected error rates after the fallback routing and batch reduction. We'll keep the fallback for a short verification window and then route traffic back once we confirm stability.

Next steps (short term):
1) Ben is leading a triage to identify whether this is a resource exhaustion (kernel/serialization) or a model-level memory fragmentation issue.
2) We'll share a recovery update within 2 hours and a post-incident summary within 3 business days.
3) If you want immediate rollback to your previous routing (no fallback), reply and we can schedule it after verification.

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing preventing recurrence and will share concrete mitigations.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachment: lodestar-4b-request-samples.txt (text, 12KB)
Attachment: lodestar-4b-cpu-metrics-20270828.csv (csv, 42KB)

Date: 2027-08-28T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lodestar-4b: 503 spike — notice + immediate mitigations

Thanks for the heads up, Irene.

We saw the elevated errors on our side — it caused a few live agent sessions to drop. Appreciate the quick diversion to the fallback. Please keep us posted if you find this is attributable to something we did (changes to request size, rate, or payload structure) — we haven't deployed anything in the last 24 hours but will check.

Can you also confirm whether our retry policy should be adjusted while the batch size is lower (we saw retries exacerbating bursts)?

— Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering
BrightBox AI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightbox.ai>, ops@brightbox.ai
Date: 2027-08-28T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Lodestar-4b: 503 spike — triage findings and immediate mitigations

Quick triage notes:
- Reproduced the spike in test harness when feeding long-context requests (>= 12k tokens) with concurrent batches of size 10+.
- Kernel logs show repeated small OOM-like reclamation events inside the runtime allocator; not full OOM, but enough to trigger request-level failure and a cascading queue stall under our continuous-batching path.
- The fallback (compat variant) uses a slightly different allocator path and avoids the high-concurrency continuous-batching optimization — that is why we saw immediate reduction in failures.

Temporary mitigations applied (now):
- Keep fallback active for 3 hours while we validate.
- Set per-account batch_size cap to 4 for routes using Lodestar-4b; we reduced BrightBox's batch size by policy to minimize surface area.

Planned next steps (engineering):
1) Priyom will push a runtime patch that adds an allocator safety check to prevent the small-reclamation cascade (staging => 2 hour smoke).
2) Marissa will run extended load tests with representative BrightBox request samples from the attached file.
3) If patch looks good, we will roll to production in a controlled canary over 4 hours with automatic rollback on p99 latency or error-rate regression.

I'll post a status update after the staging smoke (ETA 11:15 PDT).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Incident Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightbox.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, ops@brightbox.ai
Date: 2027-08-28T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Lodestar-4b: recovery update and canary plan

Hi Sarah — short update following Ben's triage:

- The runtime patch has passed our staging smoke (Priyom + Marissa ran the fixture). The allocator safety check prevents the reclamation cascade we saw in production.
- We started a canary rollout at 11:30 PDT to 8% of traffic for Lodestar-4b with additional telemetry and an automatic fallback to the compat variant on any regression. So far (30 minutes) the error rate is stable and latency is within normal bounds.
- We will expand to 25% at 13:00 PDT, 60% at 14:30 PDT, and full roll by 16:00 PDT assuming no regressions.

Customer action: no changes required on your side. Regarding retry policy — we recommend keeping the client retry backoff higher (initial backoff 400ms -> 800ms and max retries 2) while we complete the full rollout today to prevent retry storms.

I'll send a final closure once the rollout completes and we've observed 2 hours of stable behavior at full traffic.

Thanks for your patience — we'll follow up with a short postmortem and action items.

Best,
Irene
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightbox.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, ops@brightbox.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Lodestar-4b: post-incident summary and action items (INC LDST-78)

Hi Sarah / BrightBox team,

Thanks again for the coordination. This is the post-incident summary for the Lodestar-4b elevated 503s observed on 2027-08-28.

What happened (summary):
- Between ~07:45-08:20 PDT on 2027-08-28 a combination of long-context, high-concurrency batches triggered a runtime allocator reclamation cascade that produced intermittent request failures (503/timeouts) across the Lodestar-4b continuous-batching path.

Impact:
- BrightBox: ~9% of generation requests returned 503s during the window; some live sessions experienced dropped responses. No data loss.
- Internal: transient increase in p99 latency and a small spike in autoscaling activity for that pool.

Root cause:
- A subtle interaction between continuous-batching optimizations and the allocator under high-concurrency, long-context workloads. The runtime could perform frequent small reclamations that starved request handling threads, causing request errors without reaching full OOM.

What we changed (permanent fixes):
1) Runtime patch (deployed 2027-08-28): adds allocator safety checks and a guard against rapid reclamation cycles.
2) Queueing safeguard: automatic per-route batch-size caps will be enforced for Lodestar-4b for accounts with long-context profiles.
3) Telemetry: added new metrics around allocator reclamation and batch concurrency to alert at lower thresholds.

Action items and owners:
- Ben Carter: finalize allocator integration tests and expand regression suite (complete by 2027-09-08).
- Marissa Cole: run 72-hour soak for Lodestar-4b at representative BrightBox loads and report anomalies (complete by 2027-09-05).
- Priyom Das: tune automatic cap thresholds and publish updated routing policy docs (complete by 2027-09-03).

Customer guidance:
- No changes required long term. We recommend the temporary retry guidance previously shared; we have removed per-account batch caps now that patch is validated in production.

Attachments: postmortem-actions.md (action list), lodestar-4b-request-samples.txt, lodestar-4b-cpu-metrics-20270828.csv

If you'd like a synchronous walk-through of the postmortem with our engineering leads, we're happy to schedule a 30-minute call.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll continue monitoring and will notify you if any related regressions appear.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
